identity.title: Masses and Densities of Dwarf Planet Satellites Measured with ALMA

paper_type_evidence.quote: A complete description of the observations, including the method for obtaining final flux densities, is contained in BB18. We describe here only the further steps in the data reduction required to obtain the astrometric positions and errors.

question.value: Can ALMA absolute astrometry detect the barycentric wobble of Orcus and Eris from their satellites Vanth and Dysnomia, giving satellite-primary mass ratios and densities?

evidence.quote: We have used the Atacama Large Millimeter Array (ALMA) to measure precise absolute astrometric positions and detect the astrometric wobble of dwarf planet Orcus and its satellite Vanth over a complete orbit.
This paper makes use of ALMA data: ADS/JAO.ALMA#2018.1.00929.S, ADS/JAO.ALMA#2015.1.00810.S, and ADS/JAO.ALMA#2016.1.00830.S.
This paper makes use of ALMA data: ADS/JAO.ALMA#2018.1.00929.S, ADS/JAO.ALMA#2015.1.00810.S, and ADS/JAO.ALMA#2016.1.00830.S.
This paper makes use of ALMA data: ADS/JAO.ALMA#2018.1.00929.S, ADS/JAO.ALMA#2015.1.00810.S, and ADS/JAO.ALMA#2016.1.00830.S.

method.value: Direct visibility fits: two point sources for Orcus/Vanth, limb-darkened disk for Eris; initial positions from image Gaussian fits

evidence.quote: In the case of Orcus and Vanth, we use a model of two point sources, with initial position estimates given by Gaussian fits to the images.

method.value: RSS of formal fit error, systematic fit error (visibility vs Gaussian image positions), and celestial-frame error from check-source offsets

evidence.quote: We then take the total error in either direction (right ascension or declination) as the root sum squared (RSS) of those three values.

method.value: 6-parameter likelihood model: phase offset, mass ratio, 2D ephemeris offset, 2D ALMA-optical center-of-light offset

evidence.quote: we fit the deviations of Orcus and Vanth from the expected system ephemeris position to a 6-parameter likelihood model

key_parameters.value: 100000 samples after burn-in; median and 15.9/84.1% intervals

evidence.quote: After an initial burn-in, we collect 100000 samples of the Markhov chain (MCMC) for analysis.

fitting.value: MCMC with emcee; priors not stated

evidence.quote: We evaluate this 6-parameter model using the Markhov Chain Monte Carlo method implemented in *emcee*

method.value: 3-parameter MCMC (barycentre offset plus 2D ephemeris offset) using Eris positions only

evidence.quote: Our model thus only has 3 parameters, the barycenter offset and the two-dimensional ephemeris offset.

fitting.value: MCMC; reported as 1 sigma upper limit

evidence.quote: we chose to instead report the derived mass ratio as a 1$\sigma$ upper limit of 0.0084 also corresponding to a 3$\sigma$ upper limit of 0.015
with a reduced $\chi^2$ value of 1.8

method.value: Two-source visibility fit of 2018 Band 6 data; add flux to BB18 thermal model

evidence.loc: The size and density of Dysnomia
evidence.quote: We fit visibilities to a two-source model and find flux densities of $390\pm7 \mu$Jy for Eris and $45\pm7 \mu$Jy for Dysnomia.

validation.value: Fitted positions insensitive to initial model positions

evidence.loc: The size and density of Dysnomia
evidence.quote: the final fitted positions for Eris and Dysnomia are insensitive to their positions in the initial model provided to the fit

method.value: Mass ratio times system mass; density from diameters

evidence.quote: For diameters of Orcus and Vanth of 910$^{+50}_{-40}$ and 475$\pm$75km and a system mass of $6.32\times10^{20}$ kg
for a system mass of 1.65$\times10^{22}$ kg (cite: 2021Icar..35514130H) the 1 $\sigma$ upper limit to the mass of Dysnomia is $1.4\times 10^{20}$ kg.
using the Markhov Chain Monte Carlo method implemented in *emcee*
we find a Vanth-Orcus mass ratio of 0.16$\pm$0.02
corresponding to a mass ratio of 0.0050$\pm$.0035

findings_qualitative.value: Orcus-Vanth likely reached double synchronous state; Vanth is a largely intact impactor

evidence.quote: consistent with the hypothesis that Vanth is a largely-intact impactor from a giant collision in the system

claims.hypothesis: Does Vanth have a high mass ratio like a Pluto-Charon analogue?
claims.experiment: Astrometric wobble fit of Orcus/Vanth over 4 epochs
claims.finding: Highest mass ratio of any known planet/dwarf planet; consistent with intact giant impactor

evidence.quote: This 10$\sigma$ detection of barycenter motion directly shows that Vanth contains 13.7$\pm$1.3% of the mass of the system

claims.experiment: Eris wobble limit plus 2018 Band 6 detection
claims.finding: Dysnomia is significantly less dense than Eris

evidence.quote: We find that Dysnomia has density of $<1.2$ g cm$^{-3}$, significantly lower than the 2.4 g cm$^{-3}$ of Eris.

alternatives_considered_or_rejected.value: Eris 1.5σ barycentre motion not claimed as detection; reported as upper limit

evidence.quote: While this barycentric motion may represent a true detection, we chose to instead report the derived mass ratio as a 1$\sigma$ upper limit of 0.0084

limitations_admitted.value: Two Orcus epochs have much larger errors due to poor conditions and compact configuration

evidence.quote: The observation on October 13 was impacted by poor observing conditions; that on November 7 was taken when antennas had been moved into a more compact configuration.

referee_caveats_inferred: Eris result is only 1.5σ, upper limit choice is subjective
Density depends on large diameter uncertainties from thermal modelling
Only four Orcus epochs, two with large errors
Mismatch: abstract upper limit 0.0085 vs text 0.0084
